quests.title: The Stranded Garrison
quests.description:
Watchwarden Kelgrim. Keep low coming up - they've got rifles on that wall and too much time.

I've held this post longer than I'm willing to put a number to.

The humans washed up here years back. Kul Tiras sailors - shipwrecked, marooned, nobody's ever got a straight answer out of a survivor before putting him down, and I include myself in that.

They dug in. Built walls out of the keep's old stones, which I'll admit was good work.

Now they raid the coast road when they're hungry, and they are hungry often.

I don't call them monsters. I'm careful about that word and I'd ask you to be too.

I call them the stranded.

Thin the outer wall. Marines, deckhands, whoever's standing the watch.

And leave the one who commands them. Not out of mercy - because that conversation deserves better than me shouting it at you between sword-swings.
quests.accept_text: The outer wall. Whichever kind you find first. Don't go near the one who commands them - not yet.
quests.turn_in_text:
Good. You didn't hesitate, which tells me something about you, though I couldn't say what yet.

Sit a moment before you go back in.

There's still the matter of their captain.

quests.title: The Line You Cross
quests.description:
[Kelgrim takes his time.]

Captain Thalenvorde commands what's left of that garrison, and I've been putting this conversation off since you first walked up here.

Here's the whole of it.

Thalenvorde is a person.

Not a boar. Not a demon pulled out of a tear in the world that was never going to have a name until somebody asked. A person, with a rank and a crew and - however he ended up on this coast - a life before it that I'd guess looked fairly ordinary.

I've killed enough of the stranded that it stopped having weight for me years ago. I'm not proud of the arithmetic and I'm not ashamed of it either.

But killing a beast doesn't ask anything of you. Killing a person does.

I'm not going to talk you out of it. The garrison won't stop raiding while he commands it, and out here that's reason enough.

I just wanted you walking in knowing what you're about to do, rather than finding out afterward.

That's the only kindness I've got today.
quests.accept_text: Inside the keep, at the heart of the garrison. He bleeds the way you do.
quests.turn_in_text:
It's done, then.

I can see it on you. That particular quiet that comes after - I remember mine, if you can believe an orc admitting to it.

He won't be leading raids on the coast road. The valley's safer for it. That part is true and it matters.

Keep what you took off him. Not as a trophy. As a reminder of where you stand now, if you find you need one.

You crossed a line today that doesn't uncross. Most of us out here crossed it a long time before you got here.

Now you know what it actually weighs. That's not nothing, and I won't pretend it is.

quests.title: Ashgrym's Old Enemy
quests.description:
Bloodwarden Ashgrym. You'll have come up from the valley, so you've met these people already - you just don't know it yet.

That Burning Blade coven you cut out of the ridge down there? That wasn't the cult. That was the part of it that wandered too far from the nest and got sloppy.

Skull Rock is the nest.

Searing Blade scouts and raiders work the approach, and they work it properly - overlapping patrols, relief points, the lot. Somebody down there has training.

Clear the approach before anyone goes near that cave mouth. I mean that as an order rather than a suggestion, because the cave is worse and I would rather you walked into it without half the patrol already shouting.

I've fought this cult before.

[He does not say how it went.]

Don't rush it.
quests.accept_text: The approach below the cave mouth. Clear it before anyone goes in.
quests.turn_in_text:
The approach is quiet. It won't stay that way once you're inside - nothing about Skull Rock stays quiet long - but you've earned the right to try.

Two names matter down there. Neru Fireblade and Gazz'uz.

Neither will make this easy.

quests.title: Fireblade
quests.description:
Neru Fireblade holds rank in that cave through fire and will, in that order.

She commands the enforcers and the warlocks in the outer chambers, and she will not be reasoned with. I know that for a fact rather than an assumption.

[A pause that goes on slightly too long.]

Old business. Older than you'd guess to look at me, and I'd rather leave it there if it's all the same to you.

She fights with fire and she fights smart, which is a far worse combination than either on its own. Most fire-throwers lose their heads when a fight turns. She doesn't.

So: don't stand still.

Whatever else you do in that room, don't stand still.
quests.accept_text: The outer chambers of Skull Rock. She'll have the enforcers and the warlocks with her.
quests.turn_in_text:
Neru's gone.

I won't pretend that's simple for me to hear.

Gazz'uz is still down there, and he's the real reason this cave has never actually closed. He's not orc, or troll, or anything that bleeds the way we do.

Be ready for that. I don't know how a person gets ready for that, but be ready for it.

quests.title: What the Cave Was Guarding
quests.description:
Gazz'uz is a demon.

I'm going to keep using that word rather than a softer one, because every softer one I've tried has made somebody treat it as less than it is and then go down there underprepared.

Not a person who crossed a line. Not a beast that grew too large. Something summoned - something tearing at the world from a place that was never meant to touch it.

That's why this cave has never closed. You can kill every cultist on that approach and the cult comes back, because the thing they're coming BACK FOR is still breathing in the dark.

It won't bleed the way Neru did and it won't stop the way a person stops.

Everything about it is wrong in a way I've never found good words for, and I've had years to try.

Kill it anyway. That's the job whether or not I can explain what it is.

And then Skull Rock is finally just rock.
quests.accept_text: The deep chamber of Skull Rock. It won't stop the way a person stops.
quests.turn_in_text:
It's over. Skull Rock is just rock - no cult, no demon, nothing down there but the echo of what used to be.

I've wanted this day for a very long time, and I mean that more literally than you'd assume.

Whatever that thing was carrying is yours. Take it, and don't look back at the cave mouth on your way out.

quests.title: Feathers for the Ledger
quests.description:
Hey. HEY. You walk, don't you? Excellent. That's the whole qualification.

Fitz. Gazlowe's cousin, which I lead with because it opens doors and costs me nothing.

I've got a buyer in Orgrimmar who pays well - properly well - for sunbaked vulture feathers. Something to do with fletching contracts.

I've never actually asked what for. I know the going rate, the going rate is good, and a question has never once improved a margin.

So here's the arrangement: you brave the Red Wastes, you collect, I cut you in fair.

Good condition, mind. No scorch marks. The buyer is unaccountably picky about scorch marks and that is another thing I have declined to investigate.

I'd go myself. I'm built for ledgers and the vultures are built for the opposite.
quests.accept_text: Out on the Red Wastes. Good condition - no scorch marks.
quests.turn_in_text:
Perfect condition, every one.

I don't know what a fletcher in Orgrimmar wants with this many vulture feathers and at this point I have made peace with not knowing.

Here's your cut.

quests.title: Scouting the Prowler Den
quests.description:
Borka. The Watchful, they call me, which started as a joke about my posting and has since become a job description.

The prowlers are denning closer to the road than they should. Three seasons I've watched these cats and they've always kept to the deep ground, and now they haven't.

I'd rather know exactly where before Razor Hill sends anyone in after them properly, because Razor Hill's idea of going in after something is forty orcs and a lot of shouting.

The den's in the dry basin west of the highway. Roughly halfway between the Orgrimmar gate and Razor Hill.

Get close enough to confirm it. Then get out.

I'm not asking for a fight. I'd rather have a live scout with an answer than a dead hero with a guess, and I have had one of each.
quests.accept_text: North of here, the dry basin west of the highway. Confirm the den and get out.
quests.turn_in_text:
Good. Now we know where they've dug in instead of guessing off droppings and torn ground.

That's worth considerably more to me than another dead prowler would have been.

quests.title: Eyes on the Road
quests.description:
Outrider. I watch this highway for a living and for three weeks the highway has been watching back.

Rustfang hyenas. They've started tailing the caravans out of Orgrimmar - hanging a hundred paces off the last wagon, never closing, picking off whatever falls behind.

That's not scavenging. Scavengers take what's already down. This is a pack that has worked out a caravan produces stragglers if you simply wait.

Wagons are running late. Two drivers have quit outright, and one of them had thirty years on that road.

I'd deal with it myself. The gate is mine to hold and somebody has to be seen holding it, which is a sentence I've grown to resent.

They're out on the Wastes either side of the highway. Threes and fours, rust-red, grinning like they know something.

They do not know anything. Make that clear to them.
quests.accept_text: Either side of the highway, out on the Red Wastes.
quests.turn_in_text:
Fewer on the road already - I can hear it. Quiet, I mean.

There's a bigger one, though. The drivers talk about him the way they talk about a tax collector.

Take this and keep your eyes open.

quests.title: Wanted: Old Redtooth
quests.description:
Every pack has a head and the Rustfang's is the one the drivers call Old Redtooth.

Scarred muzzle. One ear torn down to a notch. Bigger than a pony, and smarter than a fair number of the guards on this gate, which I'd deny saying.

Here's what makes him a bounty and not a nuisance: he doesn't charge.

He circles. He waits. He lets the others bleed you first and comes in when you've stopped counting them.

There's been a price on him since before some of these recruits were weaned. Three different gate captains have put it up and all three left it unpaid.

He keeps to the open ground off the gate road.

And don't fight him with your back to a hill. He'll have two friends up on it before you've finished having the thought.
quests.accept_text: Open ground off the gate road. Don't fight him with your back to a hill.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's the notch, right there. Redtooth's done.

Good. Keep the pelt if you want it - but I think you'll want what he was guarding more.

quests.title: Scorpid Season
quests.description:
Sentry. My beat cuts across the east side of the highway and every year about now the armored scorpids come out from under their rocks.

To mate, or to fight. I've been walking this beat six years and I have honestly never established which, and I've watched them do it at close range more often than I'd choose.

What I'm clear on is that my boots are not made for it.

They don't hunt you. That's the thing people get wrong about them - there's no malice in a scorpid.

They just do not move out of your way, and there is no arguing with a thing that simply hasn't got a concept of you.

Thin them out before they spread onto the road proper, because a wagon horse meeting one of those is a wagon in the ditch.

Out past the road, by the rock shelves. The plates are thick - go for the gaps.
quests.accept_text: Past the road, near the rock shelves. Hit the gaps in the plates.
quests.turn_in_text:
Quieter already. I'll walk the whole beat in peace for a week.

Take something out of the stores. Orgrimmar won't miss it, and if it does, it'll blame me.

quests.title: A Warm Blanket
quests.description:
Sit down, friend. I'll tell you something and then I'll ask you something.

Grosk. I've crossed these Wastes more times than I can count and I have never once been cold.

That's not toughness. It's blood, and luck, and a lifetime of walking.

And because I've never been cold, it took me three nights to notice that Grukk's boy is.

Three nights. The desert freezes after dark - properly freezes - and that child has been sleeping on a bedroll thin enough to read a letter through, about forty paces from where I lay perfectly comfortable.

I'd hunt the pelts myself. I've got too many knees for it now, and that's the plain truth rather than a joke.

Prowler pelts are the warmest thing for a hundred miles. The big sand-coloured cats, out in the rough ground west of the highway.

Good ones. No holes. He's small, but he's not that small.
quests.accept_text: Durotar prowlers, in the rough ground west of the highway. No holes in the pelts.
quests.turn_in_text:
Look at that. Asleep already and I've not even tucked it in.

You've done a better thing than most people manage all year.

I'll not be needing this anymore - the road gave it to me, and it's given you the better deal.

quests.title: The Rumble Below
quests.description:
Ridgewatch Kurr. Stand on this side of me - the sound comes round that shoulder of rock and it'll take your ears off.

I've watched Thunder Ridge for years. It has never been this loud.

Thunder lizards and the thunderhides with them are coming down off the slopes in numbers I've not seen, crowding the approach to the cave and snapping at anything that gets between them and the water.

That's not a migration. Lizards don't migrate downhill into a crowd.

They are coming down because something up there is worse than being down here, and that's the part I keep turning over at night.

Thin the traffic on the approach before whatever it is follows them down.

North-west of the highway, up the gravel basin. You'll hear them well before you see them.

And if the ground hums, step to the side. I'm serious about that one.
quests.accept_text: North-west of the highway, up the gravel basin. If the ground hums, step aside.
quests.turn_in_text:
Better. Not good, but better.

You'll have noticed the other ones up there, though. The ones that talk.

That's the real problem. Finish what you started.

quests.title: Stormbinders
quests.description:
The lizards aren't coming down on their own. I want to be exact about that because I spent a month assuming they were.

Something is feeding the storm on that ridge.

Ridge Stormbinders. I've watched them from the shoulder with a glass - they stand at the cliff edge with their arms up and they chant, and every single time they finish, a flock of static hatchlings spills out of the rocks like the stone laid them.

They're not summoning the hatchlings. I'm fairly sure of that. The hatchlings are a side effect.

Which means whatever they ARE building toward is bigger than anything I've seen come out of those rocks, and I do not want to be standing here when it arrives.

Higher up the ridge, where the rock goes dark.

Binders first - the hatchlings stop swarming when the chanting stops.

And don't stand in anything that's glowing. Anything at all.
quests.accept_text: High on the ridge, where the rock goes dark. Binders first.
quests.turn_in_text:
Quiet. Truly quiet.

Which means he's awake.

Rumblejaw. The big one. I've never seen him come down off the shelves, but I've heard him through the stone my whole posting.

quests.title: Wanted: Rumblejaw
quests.description:
Right. Rumblejaw.

There's a lizard up on those shelves the length of two ox-carts with a jaw that cracks stone. Not chips it. Cracks it - I've put my hand in the marks.

The scouts named him for the obvious reason. You feel him before you hear him, and you hear him well before you see him, and by then you've generally decided to be elsewhere.

He's never been seen past the high shelves. That was the one comfortable fact about him and I built ten years of this posting on it.

It isn't true anymore. The stormbinders have been feeding him.

So he's coming down eventually, and I'd rather it was on a day we chose.

Top of the ridge, the rock shelf above the basin.

And here's the only thing worth knowing about that fight: when the ground stops shaking, he's about to hit you.

Move when it stops. Not when it starts.
quests.accept_text: Top of the ridge, the rock shelf above the basin.
quests.turn_in_text:
Rumblejaw's down? I can hear the quiet from here.

That's the first real silence this ridge has had in ten years.

Take whatever fits.

quests.title: Cinders on the Wind
quests.description:
Cover your mouth coming up the path. I've stopped noticing the ash and that's not something to be proud of.

I've stood this cliff above the approach long enough that I'd stopped seeing it at all - and then this morning it came up the path in clouds and I remembered what clean air was.

Burning Blade torchbearers are burning their way across the approach. Not randomly. They're clearing ground, in lines, for something they intend to put there.

And a swarm of cinder imps follows them to feed on the embers, which tells you the burning isn't incidental either. You don't get a following like that off an accident.

If that fire reaches the road the Wastes burn for a week and Razor Hill eats dust all winter.

Down the cliff path, toward the cave mouth.

Torchbearers first - they light everything they pass, so every one still standing is making more work.

The imps are small and quick and they bite where you aren't looking.
quests.accept_text: Down the cliff path toward the cave mouth. Torchbearers first.
quests.turn_in_text:
The wind's clean for the first time since spring. I could cry. I won't, but I could.

There's a man down there with dogs. Kraygh.

He lit the first fire. Finish it.

quests.title: The Houndmaster
quests.description:
Houndmaster Kraygh keeps his dogs on the approach and his whip in his hand, and in four months of watching I have never once seen him sleep.

I've looked for it. I've come up here at every hour there is specifically to catch him asleep, because a man who doesn't sleep is a different problem from a man who does.

The Burning Blade bring him fresh hounds up out of the caves and he sets them on any traveller who looks too far in. Not on raiders. Not on soldiers. On travellers, specifically, because a traveller doesn't come back with friends.

He's good with a whip. He's better with an excuse - I've heard him give three to his own people from up here.

I want him gone before those hounds find a way down to the road.

Down by the cave mouth, with his pack. Cut the guards first - they hold the hounds until he gives the word.

And when the whip cracks, run. Not away. Past him.
quests.accept_text: By the cave mouth, with his pack. Cut the guards first.
quests.turn_in_text:
The whip's silent. Do you hear that? Nothing's barking.

Take his things. He won't be wanting them.

quests.title: All That Glitters
quests.description:
Fitz again. Different scheme, same excellent instincts.

Six months I've been mapping these mesas for ore. Six. And I have found exactly one thing worth writing down, and it is not a vein.

The stonebiters chew it.

Big rock-coloured brutes that gnaw the mesa edges all day, and somewhere down that extraordinary digestive tract they concentrate glittering ore. Concentrate it, mind - it comes out better than it went in.

I would dearly love to know how. I've drawn diagrams. I've shown the diagrams to people who then stopped returning my letters.

What I'd love more is a sample without going near the teeth.

Big, grey, hungry. They drop little glittering chunks when you open them up - yes, I know exactly how that sounds and I'd ask you to consider the margin instead.

Finder's cut, and no questions from me.
quests.accept_text: Mesa stonebiters, out on the mesa edges.
quests.turn_in_text:
Oh, that's lovely. It's practically jewelry.

Don't tell Gazlowe, he'll want a cut.

Here - and take one of my spare prospecting finds for your trouble.

quests.title: Hands on the Farm
quests.description:
One eye on the road and the other on Rocktusk Farm. That's the posting, and the farm is the half that keeps me up.

That was a homestead. Orcs built it, worked it, and lost it - and the quilboar didn't burn it, which is the detail I can't get past.

They moved in. They've kept the furrows. They put the previous owners' razorbacks back to work, in the same pens, on the same slop schedule.

The farmhands are quilboar who've learned that a pitchfork works on people as well as it works on earth. The tamed razorbacks have learned much the same thing from the other end of it.

Neither is a good neighbour and both are getting braver about the road.

South-west, through the gate in the palisade.

The farmhands patrol the furrows. The razorbacks follow whoever's holding the slops.

So don't be holding the slops. That's not a joke, people do it to see what happens.
quests.accept_text: South-west, through the gate in the farm palisade.
quests.turn_in_text:
Farm's quieter. Mostly.

There's a sow in the back barn - the Matron. She's been breeding war-pigs in there since spring.

I want her to stop.

quests.title: Wanted: Matron Sowbelly
quests.description:
She was an ordinary sow. I want to start there, because everyone who sees her assumes she came out of the ground that way.

The farm's breeding stock. I watched her being led in off a cart six years ago and I couldn't have picked her out of a pen.

Then the quilboar fed her whatever it is they feed things.

Now she's the size of a cart and twice as bitter, and the whole farm has arranged itself around her. The razorbacks follow her. The farmhands pray to her - I've watched them do it, in rows, at dusk.

That's the part that makes this urgent rather than unpleasant. She isn't livestock anymore. She's the reason they stay.

I want her gone before she decides the road is next.

Back of the furrows, in the barn.

She hits hard and she smells worse. Don't fight her in the open - the razorbacks will join in and they will not hesitate.
quests.accept_text: The barn at the back of the furrows. Don't fight her in the open.
quests.turn_in_text:
Matron's down.

That's a great deal of bacon, though I wouldn't touch it and I'd think less of anyone who did.

Take the good stuff. She's done with it.

quests.title: Net and Hook
quests.description:
Sylthressa Windmourne. Don't touch the bolts, your hands are - well. Don't touch the bolts.

I import silk. From places I pronounce correctly and you would not, which I say without malice and with total confidence.

I also import it, regrettably, through Scuttle Coast.

The murlocs have taken to stringing nets clean across the beach. Not for fish, as far as I can establish - there's nothing in them. They string them, and then the saltcrust crabs move into them and live there, and the whole arrangement becomes a sort of fortification nobody designed.

My caravans arrive late, tangled, and mildly crab-flavoured.

Do you understand what crab does to white silk? I have three bolts I can only sell by lamplight.

East, on the shore. The netcasters throw first and ask questions never. The crabs simply pinch.

Clear both and my silk arrives dry.
quests.accept_text: East, on the Scuttle Coast shore. Netcasters and the crabs in their nets.
quests.turn_in_text:
Dry silk! You have no idea what that means to me.

And there's something else on that coast. A murloc with a hook - my drivers call him the Net-Cutter.

Please do him next.

quests.title: Wanted: Gillfin the Net-Cutter
quests.description:
Every murloc tribe has one that learned to use a blade. On Scuttle Coast it is Gillfin, and he has rather run away with the idea.

He cuts nets. He cuts lines. When he is bored - and I believe he does get bored, which is the unsettling bit - he cuts the traders' ropes while the wagons are still loaded.

My drivers swear he took a wagon wheel once. Took it. Not broke it, not rolled it into the surf. Took it, for the hub, and left the rim.

I have stopped arguing with them about whether that happened, because three of them tell it the same way and two of them don't speak.

I would like him out of business, and I am choosing that phrase deliberately, because he is running one.

Shoreline, east. He moves between the netted rocks.

And he'll mend himself if you give him the room. Don't give him the room.
quests.accept_text: The eastern shoreline, among the netted rocks. Don't let him mend.
quests.turn_in_text:
The Net-Cutter is done? Gods.

I could kiss you. I won't - business first - but I will pay you extremely well in finery.

quests.title: Kolkar Reckoning
quests.description:
Wyll Marrow. Cartwright, out of Stormwind, and yes, I know exactly how that sounds standing here.

The Kolkar took my caravan at the Crag. Took all of it, and left me alive as an afterthought - not as mercy, I want that understood. I wasn't worth the second pass.

The Horde found me two days later, half-starved and swearing. I've never quite forgiven them for the rescue.

I'm aware that's unfair. I've had a year to work on it and it hasn't shifted.

What I have no trouble at all being clear about is the centaur.

The Crag is the bowl south-west of the Barrens road. The war-riders ride it in circles like they own it.

Fair enough. They do.

Thin them out and I'll sleep easier, which is a thing I have not done properly since the ambush and would like to try again.
quests.accept_text: The Crag - the bowl south-west of the Barrens road.
quests.turn_in_text:
There. Somewhere in a Stormwind graveyard my brother's smiling.

There's one of them I can't get out of my head. A lame one, with a limp he hides.

Bloodhoof. He broke my wagon.

quests.title: Wanted: Bloodhoof the Lamed
quests.description:
The Kolkar tell stories about their outriders. About the one called Bloodhoof they tell them quieter, and I've had that confirmed by a prisoner who had no reason to flatter him.

A crippled rider. Withered foreleg, and he kept charging anyway - long after any sensible centaur would have taken a tent and a pension and let the young ones ride.

He has taken more caravans than the rest of the Crag put together. That's not a guess, that's the Orgrimmar road ledger, and I've read it twice because I didn't believe it the first time.

I'd like him on his back in the dust, where he put the wagons.

I'm not going to tell you that's noble. It's a cartwright wanting a thing settled.

He rides alone, at the edge of the Crag where the ground drops away.

He hits like a cart and runs like a deer.

So don't chase him. Make him come to you - he will, he always does, it's the one thing that foreleg never taught him.
quests.accept_text: The edge of the Crag, where the ground drops. He rides alone.
quests.turn_in_text:
Lamed Bloodhoof's down.

I almost feel for him. Almost.

Take whatever he carried. He won't be riding again.

quests.title: Last Words
quests.description:
[The bones by the shore are a wagon-driver's. Sun-bleached, undisturbed, laid out the way a man lies down rather than the way a man falls.]

His hands are closed around two things.

A sealed letter, the wax still whole. And a cracked signet ring that is far too fine to have been his - heavy, old work, with a crest worn down past reading.

The letter is addressed to someone named Tamsin, care of the burnt caravan on the highway south-west of the traveller's camp. The hand is shaky. It was written here, or close to it, and it was written last.

The ink has faded past saying who's expecting it, or whether anyone still is.

Nothing about this says it has to be delivered.

[The ring is warm in your palm, which the sun does not entirely explain.]
quests.accept_text: The burnt caravan on the highway, south-west of the traveller's camp.
quests.turn_in_text:
[You lay the letter among the ash, as well as it can be laid.

When you straighten up the signet is a little less cracked than it was. You are fairly sure of that. You check twice.

The wind off the Wastes carries something that might be thanks, and might be wind.]

quests.title: The Safe Road South
quests.description:
Southbound Grekka. Shift over, you're standing in my shade and there isn't much of it.

I've walked the road between Razor Hill and the Valley of Trials longer than most recruits have been alive. Thirty-one years on the same stretch of dirt and I could tell you where every pothole is by the sound of my own feet.

Lately I can't get past the Rocktusk Farm turnoff without a quilboar scout shaking me down for the privilege.

And I can pay. That's not the issue. I've got a purse and a bad temper and I've handed over worse.

The issue is who else comes up that road.

Green recruits, every week, walking out of that valley with everything they own on their back. They shouldn't start their first week on the Wastes with their coin already gone.

The road south of the gateway, near the farm.

The scouts watch from above. The geomancers throw rocks from behind - take those first if you can find them.
quests.accept_text: The road south of the gateway, near the farm. Geomancers first if you can find them.
quests.turn_in_text:
You're a good one.

Now the new ones get a clean road and I get to keep what I earn.

Here - a spare out of my own pack.

quests.title: Road Tax
quests.description:
Wandering Bok. Buy something, or don't, but hear me out either way.

I sell what I can on the road between Razor Hill and the gate, and I pay the Orgrimmar road tax out of my own pocket like an honest orc.

The quilboar have started paying it too. Collecting it, I mean.

And here's how I know it's mine: every time somebody gets past them, the little leather pouches turn up in their packs afterward. Quilboar-sized. Stitched the way nobody on this road stitches.

They're not keeping coin in them for the fun of it. They've got a system. They've got a system better than mine, which I'd like on the record as the thing that actually offends me.

So that's my coin, by any reading of the ledger I'm prepared to accept.

Razormane quilboar, out on the Wastes. Pouches on their belts - you'll know them.

Bring them back and I'll consider the tax paid.
quests.accept_text: Razormane quilboar, out on the Wastes. Pouches on their belts.
quests.turn_in_text:
My coin! Smaller than I remembered, but still mine.

Now take a cut. You've earned it, and I always pay my debts.
